The Spell of Return is an Instant Spell of the Arcane Realm . This spell behaves very differently from all others. It may only be cast if a Wizard has been banished from the world due to an enemy conquering their Fortress Town. It is in fact the only spell that can be cast in this situation, and its casting will begin automatically if the player is not defeated instead. The Spell of Return has a Casting Cost of 1,000 and, if successfully cast, allows the Wizard to choose a friendly Town in which to place their new Fortress and Summoning Circle . If no Town were available, the Spell of Return would fail - therefore, a Wizard is actually defeated when their last friendly Town is lost, and never completes the Spell of Return at all.

effects_text: Regeneration is one of the many Unit Abilities available in Master of Magic . The Regeneration ability gives a unit several extremely useful advantages, and is often considered one of the best Unit Abilities in the game. During combat, whenever the Regenerating unit is injured, it will regain exactly 1 Hit Point at the end of each turn. Multi-Figure units may even recover lost Figures as a result of this automatic healing. If the Regenerating unit survives a battle, it is then completely healed of all Damage . Multi-Figure units will also regain all lost Figures as a result. In addition, if the Regenerating unit is destroyed during battle, but its army manages to win that battle, the unit is automatically restored to life - with full health as described above! Finally, the unit will completely ignore spells that would cause it direct Conventional Damage on the overland map. Exactly 9 units in the game possess Regeneration by default. 6 of these are Normal Units from the Troll race, while the other 3 are Fantastic Units . However, it is possible to give Regeneration to any unit, by casting the Regeneration Unit Enchantment on it. Furthermore, Heroes may also be equipped with Magical Items possessing a Regeneration Item Power .

Description Corruption renders a targeted tile useless, in terms of benefit to any nearby town. The effect does not expire, though there are ways to purify an affected tile, removing the corruption. The corrupted tile can be seen to have a black haze on top of the underlying terrain tile, perhaps similar to how an oil spill would appear. Sources of Corruption The Chaos spell Corruption causes immediate corruption to one tile. The Chaos spell Call the Void will cause about half the tiles in the city zone to become corrupted. The Chaos spell Great Wasting will corrupt anywhere between 3 to 6 land tiles per turn. The random Great Meteor event will cause the same effect as the Call The Void spell. Purification (Removing Corruption) Purification is the act of removing corruption from a tile. There are several different ways to remove corruption: Units with the Purify ability (like Shamans and Priests ) can remove corruption by standing on the corrupted tile and using their special ability. Gaia's Blessing has a 20% chance per turn of removing corruption from a city's catchment area. Consecration removes all corruption every turn from the city's catchment area.
